channel.title: The Cold Fusion Calendar — Upcoming Anniversaries
channel.description: Yearly anniversaries of milestones in cold fusion / LENR / energy science, looking 60 days ahead.

item.title: Apr 29: State Dept. (1999)
item.description: Conference on Free Energy at U.S. State Department includes cold fusion. 1999

item.title: Apr 30: Zhang Xinwie (1991)
item.description: Zhang Xinwie et al. experience three explosions in their lab. 1991

item.title: Apr 30: Swartz (1998)
item.description: Key Experiment: Optimal Operating Point Characteristics by Mitchell Swartz. 1998

item.title: May 1: Chubb, APS (1989)
item.description: Scott Chubb organizes first session on cold fusion at an American Physical Society meeting. 1989

item.title: May 1: APS (1989)
item.description: Physicists at American Physical Society (APS) meeting hotly denounce the work of Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons. 1989

item.title: May 2: Case, Leslie (1998)
item.description: Leslie Case demonstrates deuterium gas-loaded metallic-catalyst cell. 1998

item.title: May 3: Beaudette (2000)
item.description: Excess Heat How Cold Fusion Research Prevailed by Charles Beaudette is published. 2000. PDF: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/BeaudetteCexcessheat.pdf

item.title: May 3: CFN Podcast #011 (2018)
item.description: Cold Fusion Now! Podcast Ep. 011 — Dr. Vladimir Vysotskii: Biological Transmutations and Deactivation of Radioactive Isotopes. https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/ Audio: https://coldfusionnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/A_CFN_011_Vladimir_Vysotskii.mp3

item.title: May 4: Bockris (1989)
item.description: Third team at Texas A&M headed by John Bockris confirms Fleischmann-Pons Effect (FPE). 1989

item.title: May 5: Storms (1993)
item.description: Edmund Storms testifies before the U.S. House Subcommittee on Science, Space, and Technology. 1993

item.title: May 7: Bombay (1989)
item.description: Mumbai's The Indian Post reports ten teams in India replicate the Fleischmann-Pons Effect (FPE). 1989

item.title: May 8: Unknown (1989)
item.description: F-day at Electrochemical Society Meeting. 1989

item.title: May 9: F&P (1989)
item.description: Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons provide additional data at a meeting of the Electrochemical Society in Los Angeles, California. 1989

item.title: May 10: F&P (1989)
item.description: Fleischmann, Pons, and Hawkins publish errata in Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry. 1989

item.title: May 12: Navy (1991)
item.description: Navy researcher Stan Szpak et al publish on a new method of initiating the reaction that he developed using electro-deposited palladium-deuteride. 1991 ..... in Journal Electroanalytical Chemistry. *1991

item.title: May 13: Cold Fusion Now (2010)
item.description: In the midst of the BP Oil Catastrophe, Ruby Carat forms Cold Fusion Now to promote clean energy from cold fusion. 2010

item.title: May 13: CFN Podcast #012 (2018)
item.description: Cold Fusion Now! Podcast Ep. 012 — Dr. Melvin Miles: The Heat-Helium Discovery. https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/ Audio: http://www.coldfusionnow.com/podcast/Ruby-Carat-Melvin-Miles-Cold-Fusion-Now-012.mp3

item.title: May 15: Karabut, Kucherov, Savvatimova (1990)
item.description: A.B. Karabut, Ya.R. Kucherov, and I.V. Savvatimova present Cold Fusion Observation at Gas-Discharge Device Cathode. 1990

item.title: May 18: BARC (1989)
item.description: Ten teams report success replicating the FPE at cold fusion meeting at Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) near Mumbai, India. 1989

item.title: May 19: Sttorms (1990)
item.description: Edmund Storms of Los Alamos National Lab (LANL) compiles survey of 16 successes in tritium detection, 15 in neutron detection, and 19 successes replicating the FPE. 1990

item.title: May 19: ICCF-9 (2002)
item.description: ICCF-9 — International Conference on Cold Fusion held in Beijing, China. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/LiXZcondensedm.pdf

item.title: May 21: ICCF-8 (2000)
item.description: ICCF-8 — International Conference on Cold Fusion held in Lerici, La Spezia, Italy. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/ScaramuzzVprocofthe.pdf

item.title: May 21: JCMNS (2002)
item.description: The new field journal is named the Journal of Condensed Matter Nuclear Science (JCMNS). Archive: https://www.iscmns.org/CMNS/publications.htm

item.title: May 21: Arata-Zhang (2008)
item.description: Yoshiaki Arata publicly demonstrates cold fusion cell generating 25x return. 2008

item.title: May 22: labs (1989)
item.description: Case-Western Reserve, Texas A&M, U. of Florida, U. of Washington and the National Institute of Nuclear Physics at Frascati, Italy have all confirmed parts of the Fleischmann-Pons Effect. 1989

item.title: May 22: Mallove (1991)
item.description: Fire from Ice: Searching for the Truth Behind the Cold Fusion Furor by Eugene Mallove is published. https://archive.org/details/firefromicesearc0000mall

item.title: May 22: Arata-Zhang (2008)
item.description: Yoshiaki Arata of Osaka University and Yue-Chang Zhang of Shanghai Jiao Tong University publicly demonstrate cold fusion cell that generates 25 times energy return. 2008 ...for the public. 22, 2008

item.title: May 23: LANL (1989)
item.description: The Workshop on Cold Fusion Phenomenon held at Los Alamos National Lab in New Mexico is the first cold fusion conference ever held. 1989

item.title: May 25: labs (1989)
item.description: A team of Mexican scientists report confirmation of solid-state fusion. 1989

item.title: May 26: ICCF-26 (2025)
item.description: ICCF-26 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Morioka, Japan. Proceedings / info: https://www.jcfrs.org/iccf26/

item.title: May 27: Google (2019)
item.description: “Revisiting the cold case of cold fusion” published in Nature by Berlinguette, Chiang, Munday, Schenkel, Fork, Koningstein, and Trevithick — Google's four-year, $10M multi-institution program (UBC, MIT, LBNL) revisits palladium hydride excess heat and develops new measurement techniques for the field. Nature 569: 581–588. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1256-6

item.title: May 28: LANR/CF (2005)
item.description: First LANR/CF Colloquium at MIT organized by Mitchell Swartz. 2005

item.title: May 31: Gluck (1991)
item.description: Cold Nuclear Fusion in Thin Foils of Palladium by Peter Gluck and Evelina Palibroda reports finding neutrons. *1991

item.title: Jun 1: Carnot (1824)
item.description: Nicolas Leonard Sadi Carnot published first theoretical understanding of steam power in Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire. 1824

item.title: Jun 3: ANS (1997)
item.description: American Nuclear Society Annual Meeting in Orlando, Florida features Low Energy Nuclear Reactions Panel session. 1997

item.title: Jun 3: ICCF-21 (2018)
item.description: ICCF-21 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Fort Collins, Colorado, USA. Proceedings / info: https://iccf21.com/

item.title: Jun 5: Clarke, Arthur (1998)
item.description: Physicist and science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke calls ignoring cold fusion “one of the greatest scandals in the history of science.” 1998

item.title: Jun 5: CFN Podcast #024 (2019)
item.description: Cold Fusion Now! Podcast Ep. 024 — Dr. Sveinn Olafsson: Ultra-Dense Hydrogen and Rydberg Matter. https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/ Audio: http://www.coldfusionnow.com/podcast/Ruby-Carat-Sveinn-Olafsson-Cold-Fusion-Now-024.mp3

item.title: Jun 7: Mallove (1991)
item.description: Eugene Mallove formally resigns as MIT News Office Chief Science Writer. 1991

item.title: Jun 9: ICCF-23 (2021)
item.description: ICCF-23 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Xiamen University, China (online & in-person). Proceedings / info: https://iccf23.iscmns.org/

item.title: Jun 11: CETI (1997)
item.description: ABC-TV shows Good Morning America and NightLine feature Clean Energy Technology, Inc. (CETI) Patterson Power Cell on the same day. 1997

item.title: Jun 11: Swartz (2011)
item.description: LANR/CF Colloquium hosted by Mitchell Swartz held at MIT. 2011

item.title: Jun 12: Fox (1989)
item.description: First issue of Fusion Facts is published by Hal Fox announcing cold fusion is real and has commercial possibilities. 1989

item.title: Jun 16: Fusion Facts (1991)
item.description: Fusion Facts publishes a review of 242 positive papers from 23 countries. 1991

item.title: Jun 18: NCUAT (2011)
item.description: David J. Nagel forms NUCAT Energy, LLC. 2011

item.title: Jun 19: Texas A&M (1995)
item.description: First Conference on Low Energy Nuclear Reactions (Transmutations) held at Texas A&M University. (1995)

item.title: Jun 23: BARC (1989)
item.description: P.K. Iyengar and Mahadeva Srinivasan et al. measure four-fold increase of tritium from cold fusion cell. 1989

item.title: Jun 23: Cincinnatti Group (1997)
item.description: The Cincinnati Group presents a process of radioactive waste remediation and offers a LENT-1 thorium activity reduction demonstration cell as a commercial product. 1997

item.title: Jun 25: ICCF-13 (2007)
item.description: ICCF-13 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Sochi, Russia. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/BazhutovYNproceedinp.pdf

item.title: Jun 26: MIT (1989)
item.description: MIT Plasma Fusion Center holds Wake for Cold Fusion Party at 4PM claiming cold fusion is dead. 1989

item.title: Jun 26: Storms, Talcott (1989)
item.description: Edmund Storms and Carol Talcott from LANL detect tritium “in significant amounts” from Pd-D electrolytic cells. 1989

item.title: Jun 28: Bush, Eagleton (1991)
item.description: Robert Bush and Robert Eagleton report record amount of excess heat at ICCF-2. 1991
